claims.statement: For every eligible ordinary tree T and the fixed favorable-leaf selector F, with k=p-1, Q the total marked independent k-set count, M the sum of open-neighborhood sizes over those marked sets, and C the per-tag count of multiply marked independent (k+1)-sets, the aggregate identity kS=(|V(T)|-2p)Q-M-C holds. In the subcase |V(T)|<=2p, it implies S<=0.
claims.scope: Retained at the source claim's exact scope: eligible ordinary trees under x(T)+2<=p and 3p<2alpha(T)+1, using the same fixed F at all ranks. The identity is global over all selected leaf tags, including tags sharing a support. The sign conclusion is only for |V(T)|<=2p; no result is established for larger order.
claims.reason: retained: the extension incidence count is E=kU+C when C counts each multiply marked upper set once per tag; direct addability counting gives E=(n-2-k)Q-M, while S=U-Q. Substitution proves the identity, and nonnegativity proves the stated order subcase. A hand-checked eligible K_{1,20} instance confirms this subcase is realizable. The required compensation M+C>=(n-2p)Q for n>2p remains unproved, so the full primary aggregate remains open.

limitations: The identity does not establish the primary aggregate when |V(T)|>2p; the compensation inequality M+C>=(|V(T)|-2p)Q remains open.
The audit is symbolic with a hand-checked star instance; it is not an exhaustive computation or formal verification.
No external literature was searched or used.
